title: Before You Begin: Defining Statuses

children:
Before you begin defining statuses in the system, carefully review your 
 current processing for all item categories. Do any items require special 
 handling or refrigeration? Do you manage fragile, expensive or hazardous 
 items? How do you manage these unique items through your warehouse? Before 
 defining statuses in the system, identify all possible processing steps 
 required for your product.

Before you begin defining statuses in the system, please complete the 
 prerequisites.

Map out the processes for each item category. 
 Using a word processor or paper, write down the current types of 
 processing completed in your warehouse. It might be helpful to begin this 
 process by item category: how are refrigerated items handled, how are 
 fragile items handled, etc. This list should include all steps that occur 
 from the time an item enters the pool until its physically leaves the 
 warehouse.

Organize all the steps into one master list. Assign 
 a status number to each step in sequential order. The steps should be organized in the order in which they should occur; 
 for example, picking appears before packing because you must pick product 
 before packing it. Based on when they occur, assign a status number to 
 each step in the processes.

Assume that your company sells lawn and garden supplies. You have three 
 types of items that require their own processes: hazardous chemical product, 
 fragile product and regular product.

1. Map out all 
 processes for each item category. The three processing methods are defined. All the steps are listed in 
 the order that they are completed.

After all the steps are defined, they are organized based on the order 
 in which they are executed. The status numbers are assigned in sequential 
 order. After you have created this master list, you are ready to begin 
 defining statuses in the system.
